H8659I.name: Tarshish
H8659I.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H8659I.brief: Son of Bilhan from the tribe of Benjamin
H8659I.short: Tarshish was a son of Bilhan, a descendant of Benjamin.

H8659J.name: Tarshish
H8659J.desc: Persian living at the time of Exile and Return
H8659J.brief: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media
H8659J.short: Tarshish was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to King Ahasuerus's presence and held the highest positions in the kingdom.

H8659G.name: Tarshish
H8659G.desc: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
H8659G.brief: Son of Javan, great-grandson of Noah
H8659G.short: Tarshish was a son of Javan and great-grandson of Noah, associated with the ancient city of Tarshish.

H8661.name: Tartan
H8661.brief: Title of an Assyrian military commander
H8661.short: The Tartan was a high-ranking Assyrian military commander who led campaigns against Ashdod and Jerusalem.

H8674.name: Tattenai
H8674.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H8674.brief: Persian governor who questioned the Jews' authority to rebuild
H8674.short: Tattenai was the Persian governor of the province Beyond the River who questioned the Jews' authority to rebuild the temple.

H8646G.name: Terah
H8646G.desc: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
H8646G.brief: Abraham's father who settled in Haran
H8646G.short: Terah was the father of Abraham, Nahor, and Haran, who left Ur to settle in Haran.

H8657.name: Teresh
H8657.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H8657.brief: Persian official who plotted against King Ahasuerus
H8657.short: Teresh was one of two Persian officials who plotted to assassinate King Ahasuerus but were discovered by Mordecai.

H8616G.name: Tikvah
H8616G.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H8616G.brief: Father of Shallum, husband of Huldah the prophetess
H8616G.short: Tikvah, also known as Tokhath, was the father of Shallum and the father-in-law of Huldah the prophetess.

H8616H.name: Tikvah
H8616H.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H8616H.brief: Opposed Ezra's reforms regarding foreign wives
H8616H.short: Tikvah was one of two men who opposed Ezra's reforms requiring Jewish men to divorce their foreign wives.

H8640.name: Tirhakah
H8640.desc: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H8640.brief: King of Cush (Ethiopia) who opposed Sennacherib
H8640.short: Tirhakah, the king of Cush (Ethiopia), opposed Sennacherib's invasion of Judah during the reign of King Hezekiah.
H8640.meaning: “he searched out the pious: he searched out the waiter”

forms.meaning: “he searched out the pious: he searched out the waiter”

H8647.name: Tirhanah
H8647.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H8647.brief: Son of Caleb by his concubine Maacah
H8647.short: Tirhanah was a son of Caleb by his concubine Maacah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

H8656G.name: Tirzah
H8656G.desc: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H8656G.brief: Daughter of Zelophehad, granted inheritance rights
H8656G.short: Tirzah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who were granted inheritance rights in the absence of male heirs.

H8634.name: Taralah
H8634.brief: Town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin
H8634.short: Taralah, a town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin (<ref="Josh. 18:27">Josh. 18:27</ref>).

H8659H.name: Tarshish
H8659H.brief: Distant maritime city known for its wealth and trade
H8659H.short: Tarshish, a distant maritime city known for its ships, wealth, and trade, possibly located in southern Spain (<ref="1Kgs. 10:22; Isa. 23:1; Jonah 1:3">1Kgs. 10:22; Isa. 23:1; Jonah 1:3</ref>).

H8620.name: Tekoa
H8620.brief: Town in Judah, home of the prophet Amos
H8620.short: Tekoa, a town in Judah, known as the birthplace of the prophet Amos and the home of one of David's mighty men (<ref="2Sam. 14:2; 1Chr. 11:28; Amo.1.1">2Sam. 14:2; 1Chr. 11:28; Amo.1.1</ref>).

H8646H.name: Terah
H8646H.brief: Israelite campsite during the wilderness journey
H8646H.short: Terah, a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey (<ref="Num. 33:27-28">Num. 33:27-28</ref>).

H8607G.name: Tiphsah
H8607G.brief: City on the Euphrates, extent of Solomon's kingdom
H8607G.short: Tiphsah, a city on the Euphrates River, marking the extent of Solomon's kingdom (<ref="1Kgs. 4:24">1Kgs. 4:24</ref>).

H8607H.name: Tiphsah
H8607H.brief: City attacked by King Menahem of Israel
H8607H.short: Tiphsah, a city attacked and brutally conquered by Menahem, king of Israel (<ref="2Kgs. 15:16">2Kgs. 15:16</ref>).

H8656H.name: Tirzah
H8656H.brief: Canaanite city that became the capital of Israel
H8656H.short: Tirzah, a Canaanite city captured by Joshua, later served as the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel before Samaria (<ref="Josh. 12:24; 1Kgs. 14:17; 15:21, 33; 16:6-23">Josh. 12:24; 1Kgs. 14:17; 15:21, 33; 16:6-23</ref>).

H8603.name: Tophel
H8603.brief: A place near where Moses addressed the Israelites
H8603.short: Tophel, a location mentioned in Moses' speech to the Israelites, possibly near modern-day et-Tafeleh, southeast of the Dead Sea (<ref="Deut. 1:1">Deut. 1:1</ref>).

H8612.name: Topheth
H8612.brief: Site of pagan child sacrifice, south of Jerusalem
H8612.short: Topheth, located in the Valley of Hinnom (also called the Valley of Slaughter or Baca Valley) south of Jerusalem, was a site of pagan child sacrifice that was defiled by King Josiah (<ref="2Ki.23.10; Jer.7.31-32; 19:2, 6, 11-14; 32:35; Isa.30.33">2Ki.23.10; Jer.7.31-32; 19:2, 6, 11-14; 32:35; Isa.30.33</ref>).

forms.english: Valley of the Son of Hinnom

H8662.name: Tartak
H8662.brief: An Avvite deity worshipped in Samaria
H8662.short: Tartak was a deity worshipped by the Avvites, one of the peoples settled in Samaria by the Assyrian king (<ref="2Ki.17.31">2Ki.17.31</ref>).

H8654.name: Tirathite
H8654.brief: A Kenite clan skilled in scribal arts
H8654.short: The Tirathites were a Kenite clan known for their scribal skills, mentioned in <ref="1Ch.2.55">1Ch.2.55</ref> among the descendants of Salma.
